# Exact capacitated flow balance and a critical nonclosure calibration

This note tests the stationary-flow proposal from the ideation synthesis.
It supplies exact balance identities and a genuine critical example where
closure fails. It does not prove OC or rule out closure using the additional
hypotheses of a bad attained minimum and all selected critical covers.

## 1. Variance records precisely what a capacity transport leaves unpaid

Let pi be a finite compactly supported physical martingale transport from
mu to nu'<=nu. Write delta=nu-nu'>=0, and let z be the projection to the
original integer coordinates. For every a in R^n,

    integral |z-a|^2 d(nu-mu)
      = integral |z'-z|^2 d pi + integral |z-a|^2 d delta. (1)

Proof: expand |z'-a|^2-|z-a|^2 into |z'-z|^2 plus
2(z-a).(z'-z). The latter has zero integral by the source conditional
barycenter identity. Add the unused target capacity delta. All integrands
are bounded on a fixed compact set, so every term is finite. More generally
the matrix identity holds with (z-a)(z-a)^T and the increment covariance.

In particular, equality of the projected source and FULL target-capacity
marginals forces delta=0 by their total masses, and then z'=z pi-almost
everywhere. It is enough to have equality of total masses and equality of
the displayed strictly convex second moment. Equality of their FIRST
moments does not suffice. For a sum of separately labeled transports,
(1) adds with their same nonnegative coefficients and retains every
unused-capacity term; a nonzero displacement cannot cancel another one.

Thus a proposed closure needs an actual projected marginal or second-
moment balance. Calling the boundary and section first moments balanced
does not supply that missing identity.

## 2. Exact elimination of a finite barycentric flow

Let P be a finite set of DISTINCT points and f_pq>=0 a finite flow with

    a_p=sum_q f_pq, b_p=sum_q f_qp,
    sum_q f_pq(q-p)=0.

Put s_p=(a_p-b_p)_+, t_p=(b_p-a_p)_+, m_p=a_p+t_p=b_p+s_p.
At states with m_p>0 use transition probabilities T_pq=f_pq/m_p and
stopping probabilities D_p=t_p/m_p. Both options together have total
probability one; the stop remains at the current base. The barycenter of
the next or stopped base is p. Inject initial mass s_p.

Every closed nonstopping communicating class has just one base. Indeed
each coordinate is harmonic on its finite irreducible transition class.
At a maximum its average can equal that maximum only when every positive
successor is also a maximum. Irreducibility makes the coordinate constant
throughout the class; distinctness of P makes the class a singleton.
Such a singleton has outgoing mass a_p entirely on its loop and t_p=0.
Consequently b_p<=a_p, while the loop alone contributes a_p to b_p, so
b_p=a_p, s_p=0, and there is no incoming flow from another state. It may
therefore be deleted without changing any injected or terminal mass.

After deleting these isolated loops and zero states, every remaining
state can reach a positive stopping probability. Finiteness gives an
integer N and epsilon>0 such that stopping occurs within N steps with
probability at least epsilon from every state. The probability of N k
transitions is at most (1-epsilon)^k, hence absorption is certain and
the matrix sum G=sum_(k>=0) T^k converges.

The vector identity m=s+mT gives m=sG. Thus the expected total traversals
of edge pq from the injected mass equal m_p T_pq=f_pq, and the terminal
mass at p equals m_p D_p=t_p. The terminal law gives a martingale
transport from s to t: boundedness of P and the preceding geometric tail
justify passage from the finite stopped means to the terminal mean.
For a convex function phi on conv(P),

    sum_p t_p phi(p)-sum_p s_p phi(p)
       = sum_pq f_pq[phi(q)-phi(p)] >=0.                (2)

The equality is finite row/column subtraction. The inequality is rowwise
Jensen. In the quadratic case the right side is exactly
sum_pq f_pq |q-p|^2. Edge labels can be retained as the actual random
path labels; no estimate of cap rewards is inferred by discarding them.

This elimination uses only original states. It differs from truncating a
residual projection at a noninteger first-exit point, and does not assert
that a residual root is a supermartingale. It supplies neither a bound of
2^n on terminal states nor a Gamma reward at those states.

## 3. Actual globally critical R4 stress does not close at the base

Use the audited R4 product from
`candidate b78a2eb10bd3783f`.
Its base is

    P={z in Z^2: -z1-z2>=-4, 2z1-z2>=-4, 2z2-z1>=-4},

with 31 points, and every fiber is the same triangle K. Its three regular
canonical caps have common true global depth beta=40/93 and common full
section centroid (0,g_K). Let W be their equally weighted boundary profile.
The exact certificate in the cited source gives (W/beta) eta <=cx eta,
preserving each continuous normal. Thus pi from nu=(W/beta)eta to eta is
an actual stress martingale with zero unused capacity. Genuine global
criticality uses the separate all-normal certificate cited there.

Consider the facet lambda0=0, of length L. Parametrize lambda1=(r+s)/3,
lambda2=1-lambda1, with 0<r<1 and s=0,1,2. Write ell=(-z1-z2,
2z1-z2,2z2-z1), and let h_z count the tiers s for which

    number{j:ell_j>0}
       +1_{ell1=0,s>=1}+1_{ell2=0,s<=1}=2.

The only profile values are 1/3 and 2/3. Integrating the three equal-
length tiers shows that the projected coefficient of eta-nu at base z is

    L[1-(1/beta)(1/3+h_z/9)]=L(27-31h_z)/120.          (3)

For a fully checkable finite sum, the following table lists, at each
first coordinate x, the sums of c_z=27-31h_z times
1, z1, z2, z1^2, z1 z2, z2^2 over the bases on that slice:

| x | 1 | z1 | z2 | z1^2 | z1 z2 | z2^2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|-4|27|-108|-108|432|432|432|
|-3|54|-162|-135|486|405|351|
|-2|-47|94|-100|-188|200|316|
|-1|-20|20|124|-20|-124|22|
|0|-28|0|468|0|0|480|
|1|-20|-20|-82|-20|-82|64|
|2|-47|-94|-194|-188|-388|-272|
|3|54|162|27|486|81|27|
|4|27|108|0|432|0|0|

The mass and first moments vanish, but the second-moment matrix is

    integral z z^T d(eta-nu)
        = (L/120) [[1420,524],[524,1420]].             (4)

By (1), EVERY such martingale on this normal bundle has projected
displacement energy (71/3)L>0. No choice of coupling closes it. The
table is also checked by the exact short standalone verifier
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_r4_projected_stress_variance_root.py`.

This example is above its OC target 1/9 and is not an attained bad
minimum. It proves that actual global criticality, common section
centroids, regularity, complete bases, and the individual normal stress
do not themselves provide stationary projected flow. Any new closure
argument must use further information, such as the genuine bad-minimum
condition and its universal selected-cover constraints. The example does
not obstruct such a strengthened argument.
